subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Shortcut-Rewarding Problems — Tricks SSC Paper-Setters Expect You to Know (W13 B1)

questions.stem: Find the sum: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + ... + 25 (all consecutive odd numbers from 1 to 25).
questions.explanation: B is correct. SHORTCUT: Sum of first n odd numbers = n². The 25th odd number = 2×13−1=25 → there are 13 terms. Sum = 13² = 169. LONG METHOD: 1+3+5+...+25 = (13/2)(1+25)=13×13=169 ✓. Paper-setter trap: students add individually (takes 30+ seconds). The shortcut (n²) gives the answer in 2 seconds. Trap: 225 = 15² (counting 25 as the 15th odd number — wrong); 196 = 14² (miscounting).

questions.stem: If a salary increases by 25% and then decreases by 20%, what is the net percentage change?
questions.explanation: B is correct. SHORTCUT: Net multiplier = (1+25/100)(1−20/100) = 1.25×0.80 = 1.00 → EXACTLY 0% change. This is a classic SSC trap: +25% followed by −20% seems like +5% net, but it is ZERO because the 20% decrease applies to the INCREASED value. Verify: salary=100→125→100 ✓. Paper-setter intention: trap students who add percentages (+25−20=+5). The answer 0% surprises most students. Trap: +5% = naïve addition of percentage changes (wrong).

questions.stem: Two articles are sold at Rs.990 each. One is sold at 10% profit, the other at 10% loss. What is the overall result?
questions.explanation: B is correct. SHORTCUT: When two items are sold at the SAME price, one at x% profit and other at x% loss → ALWAYS a net loss of x²/100 %. Here x=10: loss% = 100/100 = 1%. Total SP=1980. Total CP: CP₁=990×100/110=900; CP₂=990×100/90=1100; CP=2000. Loss=Rs.20. 1% of 2000=Rs.20 ✓. PAPER-SETTER TRAP: most students think equal P% and L% cancel out → 0%. They NEVER do at the same SP. Trap: 'Neither profit nor loss' is the most tempting wrong answer.

questions.stem: Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are offered on a product. What is the equivalent single discount?
questions.explanation: A is correct. SHORTCUT: Net discount = a+b−ab/100 = 20+10−(20×10)/100 = 30−2 = 28%. LONG METHOD: After 20% off MP: pay 80%. After 10% off that: pay 80%×90%=72% of MP. Discount = 28% ✓. PAPER-SETTER TRAP: students add discounts: 20+10=30% (wrong). The second discount applies to REDUCED price, not original. Trap: 30% = naïve addition; 29% = arithmetic error.

questions.stem: A train 300 m long passes a pole in 15 seconds. How long does it take to pass another train of 200 m coming in the OPPOSITE direction at the same speed?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Train speed = 300/15 = 20 m/s. Opposite-direction crossing: total distance = 300+200=500 m; relative speed=20+20=40 m/s. Time=500/40=12.5 seconds. SHORTCUT for opposite-direction: relative speed = sum of speeds; total distance = sum of lengths. PAPER-SETTER TRAP: students use same speed (20 m/s) without doubling for opposite direction → 500/20=25s (wrong). Trap: 25 = correct for same-direction or ignoring relative speed; 15 = train passing a pole (single length).

questions.stem: A principal doubles in 10 years at Simple Interest. In how many years will the SAME principal become FOUR TIMES?
questions.explanation: C is correct. SHORTCUT: At SI, the interest earned is LINEAR. Doubles (1P interest) in 10 years → rate = 10%/year. For four times = 3P interest needed. Time = 3P/(P×10%) = 30 years. Formula: if it becomes n times in t years at SI, it becomes m times in t×(m−1)/(n−1) years. Here: m=4, n=2, t=10 → 10×3/1=30 years ✓. PAPER-SETTER TRAP: students think double in 10 years → four times in 20 years (true for CI, NOT SI!). SI is linear, not exponential. Trap: 20 = CI answer (wrong for SI).

questions.stem: Three taps A, B, C can fill a tank in 6, 8, and 12 hours respectively. All three are opened together. How long does it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: B is correct. SHORTCUT (LCM method): LCM(6,8,12)=24 units. A fills 4u/h, B fills 3u/h, C fills 2u/h. Together: 9u/h. Time=24/9=8/3 hours=2 hours 40 minutes. FRACTION METHOD: 1/6+1/8+1/12=(4+3+2)/24=9/24=3/8 per hour. Time=8/3h ✓. PAPER-SETTER TRAP: students use 1/6+1/8+1/12 and make fraction errors. The LCM method is faster and less error-prone. Trap: 3 hours = adds just 6+8+12 and averages (completely wrong); 4 hours = arithmetic error.

questions.stem: A person sells an article at 20% profit. Had he sold it for Rs.36 less, he would have incurred a 10% loss. Find the Cost Price.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SHORTCUT: Difference in SP = 36. SP₁ = 1.20×CP; SP₂ = 0.90×CP. Difference = 0.30×CP = 36 → CP = 120. PATTERN: When SP changes by a known amount and P%/L% flip, the difference = (P%+L%)% of CP. Here (20+10)% of CP = 36 → 30% of CP=36 → CP=120. Verify: SP₁=144; SP₂=108; 144−108=36 ✓. PAPER-SETTER TRAP: students set up simultaneous equations and waste time. The '% difference of CP = actual difference' shortcut is instant.

questions.stem: A sells to B at 25% profit. B sells to C at 20% profit. C sells to D at 10% profit. If D pays Rs.3,300, what did A pay for the article?
questions.explanation: B is correct. SHORTCUT: Total multiplier from A to D = 1.25×1.20×1.10 = 1.65. A's CP = D's price / multiplier = 3300/1.65 = Rs.2,000. VERIFY: A bought at 2000; A sold to B at 2500 (25% profit); B sold to C at 3000 (20% profit); C sold to D at 3300 (10% profit) ✓. PAPER-SETTER DESIGN: The chain of three profits with a round final price is designed to test if students know to chain-multiply and reverse. Students who work forward (and don't know the chain shortcut) waste 2+ minutes.

questions.stem: What is the unit digit of 7¹ + 7² + 7³ + 7⁴ + ... + 7⁴⁰⁰?
questions.explanation: C is correct. SHORTCUT: Unit digits of powers of 7 cycle with period 4: 7¹→7, 7²→9, 7³→3, 7⁴→1. Sum of one complete cycle: 7+9+3+1=20 (unit digit=0). 400 terms = exactly 100 complete cycles of 4. Sum of unit digits = 100×20 = 2000 → unit digit = 0. PAPER-SETTER DESIGN: 400 terms looks terrifying for brute force. The cyclicity shortcut (period-4 recognition, then notice 400÷4=100 complete cycles) gives the answer in <30 seconds. Trap: students who find the cycle but check 401 or 399 terms get wrong answers.
